title: AdaptiveByteBufAllocator: Make pooling of AdaptiveByteBuf magazine local

timeline.body:
Motivation:

To reduce the usage of FastThreadLocal and make the AdaptiveByteBufAllocator also play nice with virtual threads we should just pool the AdapativeByteBuf instances in the Magazines itself.

Modifications:

Remove usage of Recycler for pooling AdaptiveByteBuf Use a bounded MPMC queue that is stored in the Magazine itself for pooling these instances Result:

Fixes #14279

@normanmaurer I was investigating why there were test failures on https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/14332 and tried to recreate the PR from first principles. Regardless, I ended up with a very similar but slightly different implementation.
4096 felt like too many… I don't know if this is too few 😅

reply.body: Maybe just do 1024 for now ? In reality there shouldn't be too many magazines.

timeline.body: imho this usage is really odd as if this methods returns non null its a `ByteBuf` which has a lifetime. I know that this would just be the same as `into` and so its fine to not release but this is more an implementation detail and very confusing and fragile.

Like stated below I think this method implementation is fragile and confusing. Depending on if buf is null or not we might need to release the returned `AdaptiveByteBuf`. This makes lifecycle management error-prone. Let's rework this somehow

reply.body: I've been thinking a lot about the need to signal failure and the need to return a buffer, and the conflict between those two will always produce complicated code. So instead I'll try to side-step the problem by pushing the fallback paths down, and make this method infallible.

timeline.body:
I'm all in to have this - it trades the virtue of simplicity with some cost in the optimized common path i.e.
- if a thread is an event loop one it has to perform a CAS using the mpsc q to release the buffer wrapper

Another option could be to have a Recycler impl which has the same tunable we're used to AND using a pluggable concept of ownership. I'm preparing a small PoC to show what I mean

reply.body:
> if this is happening why holding the lock there's no need the q to be mpmc

This @chrisvest ?
Perhaps, but I want to have a full CI run backing up any move away from MPMC.

Here in the thread-local case, we'll go to the `Magazine.EVENT_LOOP_LOCAL_BUFFER_POOL`, which uses MPSC under the hood.

When magazines are sharable, they may be used as fallbacks, which do not involve locking the magazine.

timeline.body:
@normanmaurer @chrisvest it -> https://github.com/franz1981/netty/tree/4.1-mag-local-pool

I'm not fixing the comment at https://github.com/netty/netty/pull/14414#discussion_r1816359191 or the ones from Norman, but proposing a different fast(er)-path for event loop confined magazines (as usual :P )
I would have preferred to avoid another fasthreadlocal::get TBH, given that we already do it for the event loop-local magazine, but in this way we can reuse the `Recycler` without modifying it.
I believe there is some bench which correctly use fast thread local threads on JMH which can be used to compare against the 2.

The branch I've sent got a sole concern, perf wise:
- I made the q-based handle (shared magazines) to be an `EnhancedHandle` child (which impl the recycle methods)
- The `Recycler` already have 2 `EnhancedHandle` i.e NOOP_HANDLE and the default one
- it means that `AdpativeByteBuf::deallocate` can be megamorphic  (having 3 concrete types which can be called there)

An "easy" solution to this would be to have `AdaptiveByteBuf` to  just use an `Handle` (meaning that the shared magazines won't create a child of `EnhancedHandle` anymore, but just `Handle` - and perform an instance check on the buffer deallocate vs `EnhancedHandle` - this will make possible to have 2 call-sites:
- `Handle::recycle` which will observe a single type  i.e. the one using the queue
- `Handle::unguardedRecycle` which can observe 2 concrete types and get in the fast path of virtual call (making the JIT to emit an bimorphic guard vs the 2 types observed)

wdyt? I can add an additional commit to fix this

@franz1981 The two approaches sound equivalent in terms of code style, so we could just let the benchmarks decide. So how about we look at that in a follow-up? I know it can take lot of time to tweak benchmarks back and forth.

Right now I suggest already to bring the fast thread local solution in too - which uses array deq for the fastest path - which is very difficult to beat, unless there is something very wrong in fast thread local or elsewhere (the handle availability).
If you don't feel confident for this I can send a separate PR with the follow up changes

@chrisvest I've sent by accident my changes into your branch - now I've forcibly pushed your original commits removing mine :"( 
I'll send a separate draft PR on top of your changes here to help @normanmaurer as well to see what changes I'm proposing
